title: fix(github): publishing a checkout again updates its PR
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate pull requests when an agent publishes a local checkout, commits a follow-up such as a CI fix, and calls `github_publish(workspacePath)` again.

Related: #196168.

## User Impact

Later publications from the same conversation and canonical checkout update the existing task branch and PR. Follow-up commits, amends, and rebases—including rebases with identical file contents—retain the right PR diff. The requesting conversation keeps its original workspace, and the source checkout is unchanged.

An existing publication task from an earlier version is reused when exactly one matches. If several match, the error identifies their session keys and readiness command instead of guessing or creating another PR. Existing accepted requests retain their original task and snapshot, even when the source has newer committed or uncommitted changes.

No configuration, schema migration, or administrative binding repair is required. Existing project, requester, filesystem, and publication authorization remains; a reused task is authorized before its checkout is synchronized.

## Why This Change Was Made

#196168 separated publication custody from the initiating conversation, but keyed each task by the tool invocation's idempotency key. A fresh call therefore selected a new task, branch, and PR. This change keys new tasks by conversation and canonical checkout, gives exact accepted receipts precedence, and discovers older tasks through their recorded source checkout.

Before a fresh publication, the existing task advances with an exact-tree merge retaining the source commit's ancestry. Checking both the tree and ancestry matters: a same-tree rebase still needs the new upstream history so upstream changes disappear from the PR diff. The coordinator, receipt schema, credential owner, and GitHub publisher remain unchanged.

Accepted edge case: if a newer publication advances this task while an earlier request is queued, the earlier request can fail with the existing workspace-changed error; the newer request publishes the current work. Ambiguous historical tasks require deliberate selection because automatically choosing one could update the wrong PR.

## Evidence

- Registered Gateway-handler integration covers same PR/branch across follow-ups and amends, same-tree rebases, older-task reuse, exact retry after a rename or source changes, ambiguous older tasks, deleted tasks, project restrictions, and authorization before checkout mutation.
- The same-tree rebase, accepted-retry mutation, older-task reuse/ambiguity, dirty-source retry, and pre-sync authorization cases were reproduced failing before the respective repairs, then passed with them.
- Focused session-access, requester, tool-handoff, and publish-tool runs passed (117 tests across those suites); all 27 session-access cases passed after the retry correction, and the three affected publication/rebase/older-task cases passed again after final assertion consolidation.
- Targeted type-aware lint, core and Gateway-methods test typechecks, formatting, and diff checks passed. `pnpm build qaRuntime` passed on clean commit `d45e7cab53b72cfdfde223bf85afaacd8734de5e`; both build stamps match it.
- Fresh independent local review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Current-head CI and a hosted ClawSweeper re-review are being followed separately.

- Built-runtime proof on `d45e7cab53b72cfdfde223bf85afaacd8734de5e` uses an isolated UTM VM, real model, agent-tool/handoff, and signed registered Gateway boundaries. An ordinary unbound conversation with publication scopes and no administrative authority published, recovered an accepted follow-up after a crash/restart, and published again after a same-tree rebase. All three terminal results used one PR/branch, exactly one PR was created, and the final diff contained only the task change. Restart completion was delivered once to the initiating transcript. External GitHub effects were simulated at the transport boundary; no runtime authority owners or accepted receipts were mocked. A read-only requester was refused. After revoking an accepted requester before a GitHub write and restarting again, the queued publication failed with `identity_changed` and dispatched no push or PR creation; a fresh request was forbidden for missing `operator.sessions.write`. The source checkout stayed clean at the expected HEAD, and the initiating conversation retained its original workspace metadata. Administrative RPC remained forbidden. The model read the original workspace marker using an absolute path, so this does not claim a literal relative-path read. This proof exercises the new explicit-path flow, not an exact replay of the historical call that omitted `workspacePath`; legacy-task upgrade handling is covered by registered-handler integration tests.

The original contributor's earlier real-GitHub and package-install observations were on `24f28f8`; they are not claimed as independently verified proof of this revision. No remote test publication, production service change, merge, or deployment was performed during this follow-up.
